However, one of the convoys went from Gjakove towards Prizren while the other one went towards the village of Brekoc and then Zhur, Qafe e Prushit. However, this was not simultaneous. They were not allowed to cross on the same day, so some of them were turned back, and the Korenica convoy went towards Prizren. So these two arrows show the direction of the movement of the population in the Lugu i Carragojs, and Korenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Your Honours, I tender this pre-marked map and ask that it be received in evidence. The witness has already marked a map before the Court with these observations, and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djordjevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Could you pause, please, Mr. Djordjevic. We're not getting a translation at the moment. Your wisdom is being lost entirely.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can you hear the English booth now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Now we're all right. Please carry on.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. The Defence is opposed to having this admitted into evidence since it is obvious that the witness did not create this map because it requires a greater knowledge in computer science than the witness has, I believe. Therefore, I believe it would be inappropriate now, since we are dealing with the direct examination of the Prosecution, to have this admitted into evidence because we've already had a clean map, and then the witness, to his best -- to the best of his ability and knowledge, marked on that map everything that Mr. Stamp asked him to mark. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp, one thing is not clear to the Chamber. Who made the markings which we see on this document you now want us to receive?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: The markings, Your Honour, were made by an analyst of the OTP based on markings that this witness had drawn on a map, and this witness has accepted and has stated that he -- the markings here are his markings, in fact, and he accepts them as correctly depicting what he has to say. Your Honour, the markings here, it is for the Court, and a matter of weight be compared to what he marked in court. However, this is just a clearer map where one can see more easily the names of the places.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you have something further, Mr. Djordjevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJORDJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We've just heard from my learned friend Mr. Stamp that it was an OTP analyst that marked this -- or, rather, that enter these markings, and that only heightens my concern. So I really abide by what I said originally. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. The Chamber will receive this exhibit. The witness has previously, within the physical limitations of the electronic marking system, marked the positions and movements and described orally consistently with what now appears on this map, which is tendered merely as a clearer presentation. If there are any material differences, although none are presently apparent to me, if there are, they can be the subject of any submission about weight at -- when the Chamber comes to hear final submissions. It appears to the Chamber it would be assisted by the clarity of this presentation when it is viewed in association with the witness's over markings. It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be P00317, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I'm grateful, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: In paragraphs 86 to 88 of your statement, you said you saw two trucks taking bodies -- loaded with bodies, 20 bodies each, in each truck you said, along the Meje to Djakovica road, taking bodies away from Meje on the 29th of April, and these were escorted by a police vehicle, a Lada Niva police vehicle. Why did you say it was a police vehicle?

utterances.speaker: NIKE PERAJ
utterances.text: Because there was a policeman driving the car, and there were two or three other persons in the car wearing police uniforms. They used to drive cars that did not belong to the police or the army, civilian cars, which were mobilised, or maybe I should say confiscated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Would that be convenient time, Mr. Stamp, for the second break? If there something else you would prefer to deal with, please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I was checking off to see if I could close, but perhaps we could -- I don't want the Court to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: My experience, Mr. Stamp, in the many years of it, it's never wise to close when you're offered the chance of a break. You can then reflect on where you are and what may have been omitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I will accept your words of wisdom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I'm sure [overlapping speakers] counsel will follow that advice. We will have the second break and resume at 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Mr. Peraj, the elite unit that was in the field on the 27th and the 28th, did you at any time speak with any member of that unit?

utterances.speaker: NIKE PERAJ
utterances.text: I don't know to which elite units you're referring, the police or the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: The police.

utterances.speaker: NIKE PERAJ
utterances.text: No, I didn't speak with any member of that unit personally, but I think that Rasovic was more or less part of those elite units.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well. Let's move on. If we look at paragraph 85 of your --

utterances.speaker: NIKE PERAJ
utterances.text: I would like to make a small correction. In Nec village, in the mountains, I spoke personally with an officer who was a major by rank. He appeared to be the commander of the units there in that location.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you find out where this officer was from?

utterances.speaker: NIKE PERAJ
utterances.text: I and Perovic was -- were there, and there were two or three other police members of lower ranks, and when we explained to them that the terrain was clear, that there was no KLA presence or force there and that they could continue, one of them said, and I quote, Thank God it is so, because for me to come from Belgrade and die here in these valleys and mountains would be in vain.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: What day was this? Date, what date was this?

utterances.speaker: NIKE PERAJ
utterances.text: 28th of April, 1999, in the morning at about 9.00 a.m. Maybe it's not the exact time, but it was around this time, 9.00 a.m. in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you. If we could move to paragraph 85 of your statement. Earlier today, you told us that Major Zivkovic was not present with you and Seregj Peraj [sic] on the 27th or the 28th of April. In paragraph 85, you speak about the use of gas and gas canisters, and you say in the third sentence there: "I never saw gas canisters in Meje to confirm this allegation, but I am convinced that the Serbs used them. My colleague Major Zivkovic was an expert in chemical weapons and said that he detected something unusual in the air at the incident site." Were you present with him when he is supposed to have detected this unusual thing at some incident site, or do you know what he's talking about?

utterances.speaker: NIKE PERAJ
utterances.text: I was not present there with him, but with full responsibility I hereby state that I saw two or three canisters of small size, gas canisters, chemical gas canisters, of short-term effect, and this claim I base on the fact that my son, Mercur Peraj, who was at that time stopped in Meje was almost sprayed, but a policeman told the person who wanted to spray my son, No, no, don't do that. This person is Aleksandar Pekovic, a police from the MUP in Gjakove.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: My brother's son.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Lastly, Mr. Peraj, I'd like you to identify, if you can, some vehicles which I'd like to show you, some photographs of vehicles which I'd like to show to you. We have heard evidence about VJ vehicles, and I'd like you to tell us whether or not the vehicles depicted in the photograph which I propose to show to you are VJ vehicles and what types of vehicles they are.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Your Honours, with your leave, may I quickly show him -- it's 01325. That's 65 ter 01325. Could we zoom in a little bit, please. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: The vehicle at number 1, is that a VJ vehicle, and what type of vehicle is it?

utterances.speaker: NIKE PERAJ
utterances.text: This is a vehicle used both by the VJ and the police. It's a type of an armoured personnel carrier. I don't know the exact make and name of the transporter, but it was used both by the army and the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: How about number 2?

utterances.speaker: NIKE PERAJ
utterances.text: This is also a type of an armoured personnel carrier or transporter usually used by the infantry units. There are subtypes of this vehicle known as BRDMs.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: NIKE PERAJ
utterances.text: It was mainly used by the police during the war because the army had more sophisticated and newer types of this vehicle.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And vehicle 3?

utterances.speaker: NIKE PERAJ
utterances.text: As far as I can tell, it is a BVP type of vehicle on which short distance rocket-launchers can be mounted. It is an anti-aircraft type of vehicle used by the infantry forces and the artillery forces. In short, it was mainly used by the artillery units but also by other infantry units.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: In respect to 1 and 2, if there were -- I'm so sorry. In respect to 1 or 2, if they were used by the police, what colour would they be?

utterances.speaker: NIKE PERAJ
utterances.text: The police vehicles were usually blue, while the army ones were of the SMB type in B/C/S, which is olive-green/grey colour. However, during the war the vehicles were camouflaged so that they would not be detected from air and surface.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: What's vehicle 4? Is it a VJ vehicle, and what is it?

utterances.speaker: NIKE PERAJ
utterances.text: Number 4 is a vehicle known as Praga. At least while I was there, this was the name of the vehicle. It was sort of becoming extinct because the army was tending not to use them. They're usually used in anti-aircraft warfare.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: They are VJ vehicles, I take it, the Pragas?

utterances.speaker: NIKE PERAJ
utterances.text: Yes, they are, of the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: If you could move on to page 2. Items 5 and 6 are -- what can you say? Are they, firstly, VJ vehicles or not, and what type of vehicles are they?

utterances.speaker: NIKE PERAJ
utterances.text: Number 5 and number 6 are army vehicles, tanks. It seems to me that it's the same type depicted on both photographs, but one is camouflaged. It's the T-55 type of 100-millimetre calibre.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And 5 and 6 -- sorry, 7 and 8?

utterances.speaker: NIKE PERAJ
utterances.text: Number 6 -- 7 and 8, correction, depict military vehicles which were also used by the police. Number 7 is a vehicle type T7. It's smaller in size. It's a tank of a T7, while number 8 is known with the name of tank T11. The T7 or 8 can carry eight persons and the driver, while the other one can carry 14 persons in total.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Did you say tank T11 or TAM T11?

utterances.speaker: NIKE PERAJ
utterances.text: TAM, T-A-M, T11. It's bigger in size and was used to carry personnel and equipment depending on the need.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: If we could move to the next page, please. What types of vehicles are at 9, 10, and 11?

utterances.speaker: NIKE PERAJ
utterances.text: Number 9 is BOV vehicle usually used by the anti-aircraft artillery units. Number 10 is a type of the BOV vehicles. There are three or four different types of BOVs. I'm not an expert, but I know at that we had this type of vehicles. Number 11 also depicts a BOV vehicle used usually by the anti-aircraft units, while number 12 depicts a type of a transporter, armoured transporter.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: What is it called? Number 12, what is number 12 called?

utterances.speaker: NIKE PERAJ
utterances.text: Armoured transporter. It's very similar to the BRDM vehicle. It's a sub-type of BRDM vehicle.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I see. Now, 9, 10, 11, 12, are these military or VJ vehicles exclusively as far as you know?

utterances.speaker: NIKE PERAJ
utterances.text: Number 12 was also used by the police. We had them in the barracks in Prishtina. Ten was also used by the police, number 10, while number 9 and number 11, I don't remember seeing them as part of the equipment of the police formations. At least, personally I don't remember that they had it, number 9 and number 11.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you. If we could move to the next page, please, 13 and 14.

utterances.speaker: NIKE PERAJ
utterances.text: These are all-terrain vehicles usually used by the people from the command. As for number 15, I don't recall seeing it very often. These were used by different commanders to go to the terrain. They're all-terrain vehicles, 4 by 4. So in short, these are all-terrain vehicles with great traction power.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thirteen and 14, when you say they were used by commanders, commanders of which -- which organisations?

utterances.speaker: NIKE PERAJ
utterances.text: Both of the police and the army. Of course, the higher-ranking commanders used more sophisticated vehicles. They also used armoured transporters to go in the war zones during the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honours. I have nothing further. Oh, I always have something further. Could I tender this document and ask that it be received in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The series of 15 photographs of vehicles will be received as an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be P00318, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That concludes your examination, Mr. Stamp?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honour. It does.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, as previously indicated, the Chamber must now adjourn with a view to the cross-examination of the witness continuing on Friday. Mr. Peraj, I'm sorry, but because we have not a courtroom available tomorrow, we're having to continue on Friday, and your evidence will continue, then, at 9.00 on Friday morning. So if you'd be good enough to return then. The court officers will give you further guidance and assistance about the break, and we now adjourn to resume on Friday.
